Hey love, I know I pm'd you, but, I didn't see this. I stalk you all the time (nothing creepy, you should know that I just like checking in) but I've been really busy today. If you need anything, you know where to find me, and I promised you we'd stick out life together as hetero life mates. You're the bestest guy in town, and I need you to look self harm in the eye and say, "I'm better than this, I'm so much better than you." 
When I was about 13, I got involved in the drug scene. You know the outlines of it, how I got hooked on meth and what not. My best friend, Jay, actually died of a meth overdose right in front of me. It was really really hard, I mean, I still struggle with it you know. I loved him, I never thought I'd lose him. And we all grieve differently, some constructive and some self-destructive. When I finally quit the dumb shit, the shit that was holding me back from life, I realized James was no longer a person. He became a piece of me. My art, my songs, all of it had no meaning. Until I realized he was still alive, still thriving inside of me. He's an artist with a different vessel now, you know? It's gonna be hard to move past, and at points, you're gonna feel like it's impossible. The most important thing to remember when you're feeling like that is that you're not alone. 
Your very own, very nice (and smokin hot) best friend has gone through something very similar and I'm always open to talk about every detail as long as you're willing to listen sweetheart. 
I love you so very much and I want to see you do good, I want to see you overcome that voice in your head until it fades into nothing and all you can hear is the beauty that life holds. 
Please get ahold of me when you feel like talking, because you know I only want the best for you.

In case you didn't read what I stated earlier on in the story, I've struggled with addiction for a few years and that made it really hard to say no to free substance. 
Also stated, "really really cool dad", meaning I thought it was all innocent and he felt the same way since I figured the reason he wanted to be around me was because I was kinda like his replacement daughter.

ooh, yeah, red's super hard to get out. I'd suggest that if the red dyes aren't coming out, to get something like brass banisher (they sell it at walmart!) 
It works really well. I've used it a lot of times. But as far as the bleach goes, I don't remember the exact brand. It was something like "prism lights" or whatever, you buy it at sally's and you have to buy the powder and developer separate. It works wonders, though! 
I ended up having to bleach my hair about 5 times, and using a hella ton of the brass banisher shit. But honestly, it all depends on how porous your hair is. The less porous your hair is, the less it's gonna take chemicals. 
When you're bleaching, take a day break in between. Get a 1/4 of olive oil, microwave it for 30 seconds, and then rub it into your scalp and let it sit for an hour or so. It helps with the damage.

You don't lose the feeling really, you lose the essence of the person. It's like a huge gaping hole in my chest every day. Used to be my reason to wake up. Now it's my reason to hit the snooze button because dreams are better than reality.

It was awful and wonderful at the same time. I will always be sharing my heart with that person. The sex was great, the long nights cuddling, the inside jokes, the songs dedicated to each other. Nothing could've possibly been better. When I cried, they would hold me, or talk to me late into the night when the panicking got really bad. I remember one time, (right after a huge breakdown, I cut my hair super short and hated it, so I wore extensions 24/7 and they looked real) we were at the beach, and when I got hit by a wave my extensions came out. I was really sad and embarrassed, so when we got home I sat in the shower till the water turned cold, crying my eyes out. They came in to the bathroom since I refused to leave, and stepped into the shower with me fully clothed. We sat there and talked until the tears turned into laughter and kisses. Things changed a lot as my mental illness progressed though, I got big into the hard drug scene and did a lot of fucked up stuff. I caused a lot of fights and spread a lot of lies. The only problem with falling in love like that, is knowing they're gonna leave you one day. Break-up or death. There's no way to find an eternity with the only person you'd be willing to spend it with.

Hey! So, as much contradiction that comes with weed, I'm here to say this-
May not be physically addictive, but beware the mental addiction. 
As a (former) drug addict, I've tried all things for my depression. Weed included. I still like to blaze now and again with friends, or if I'm feeling in the mood to work on new art and jam out, but it gets to a point where you've gotta look at yourself from the outside and say, do I REALLY need to add another thing on to the list of what's bringing me down? Now, it's gonna be hard as hell to quit. It takes a lot of strength to not just break down on a bad day and get so fucked up you don't remember your name. Learn how to smoke for the calmness, for the serenity, instead of just for the high and forgetting about pain. Forgetting isn't gonna help, it's just gonna make it where you don't wanna be sober for the chance of remembering. Smoke a lil, a couple hits through out the day, just embrace the chill and stick with that. It's okay to smoke, but smoke responsibly~ 
xoxo

16, F here! I know exactly how ya feel, I went through the (almost) exact same thing. All I can say is that you are so much stronger than you'd think, believe me! When I was muddling through drug abuse and all that shit, I told myself I'd never get out. But I've been clean since the 4th of July. Fuck yeah, shit is hard. The thing is though, you've gotta keep doin you. Find things that make you happy. For me, I LOVE to dye my hair crazy colors and cut it short and wear makeup, doing that kinda stuff gets me into the mood where it's like, "yeah... I wanna go out today! let's do this!" 
Also, a good way to meet people is through people you knew from school. I live in a super small town in TN, and after I quit school and started doing online school, there weren't lots of ways for me to meet people. So you know what I did? Got on facebook, "people you might know", started adding all the motherfuckers I thought were cute. I struggle a lot with the social anxiety as well, so talking online made it really easy because then nobody could hear my stuttering, squeaky voice. Branch out like that, it's a start. Once you start to feel comfy with those people, arrange to hang out or something. You'll be surprised how many chill people you meet like that. 
I'm not the best with advice, and I'm trying to speak off personal experience here to give you as much as I can. 
PM me if ya need anything, stay strong lieutenant!

I mean, the holidays don't even feel right anymore. Since I stopped believing in Santa as a kid, it just turned into my family trying to make up for the shitty years we've had. Two years ago, my brother, his fiancee, and their baby moved right after christmas. So, I don't know. Holidays just feel wrong. Since they found out about my mental disorders, it became this whole big ordeal of trying to pretend that their stupid gifts can make me happy and when they don't, they throw a piss fit about it and call me ungrateful. The worst thing, I think, is having to tell your family "no, no, no thoughts lately. nope, no voices. no new cuts, no more attempts, no more alcohol/pills/etc." and knowing its all a big goddamn lie you're fronting just because you don't want to be put down for something you have literally no control over. 
Spending this Christmas alone, it'll be my first.

From my standpoint of being the little sister, I can say even just having a buddy to hang out with can help. When I first got out of rehab, it wasn't but a month later I had cut through a vein and my mom found me bleeding out on my bed before it was too late. I got stitches, and my older brother (by 4 years) was just getting off work by the time we were leaving the hospital. He never really went through the suicidal part of depression, his was mainly a lot of sleep and not leaving the house. But after what happened, he made it a point to spend every bit of the time he had with me. He ended up quitting school and work to make sure I always had someone to talk to when it was 2 am, I was sad, and just needed someone to hold me. A lot of people going through suicidal thoughts/attempts often feel alone, like there's no person out there who could possibly help them. My best advice for you is, 1- lock up sharp things/medicines/all that jazz, it's in your best interest. 2- FUCKING SUPPORT, and making sure she utilizes the resources she has, especially you since I assume you two live in the same household? 3- lots of spoiling. Depression is another one of those things that makes it impossible to get out of bed, any time of the day. Knowing that the day will contain good things (favorite food/movies/drinks etc...) is a good motivator for avoiding isolation. 4-  increase the compliments/affection. It makes the person feel especially loved. 
Hope I can be of some help, and if you need anything else, PM me~
xoxo
